findings.title: Raw signup body (including plaintext password) is logged before validation
findings.explanation: req.body is logged unvalidated and unfiltered. The claim that the logger redacts sensitive fields is fragile: redaction typically works on known key names at known paths, and pre-validation payloads are exactly the ones with unexpected shapes (e.g. 'Password', 'pass', 'pwd', nested objects, wrong types, extra fields, or a password sent in the wrong field such as 'email'). Any miss writes plaintext credentials and PII (email, organization) into logs, which are usually retained, shipped to third parties, and widely readable. This is a security and compliance risk (GDPR, SOC2, etc.). Instead, do not log the body. Log safe metadata only: the set of keys received, the types of values, content-type, body size, and the validation error.

findings.title: Debugging goal is better solved by logging the validation failure, not the input
findings.explanation: signupSchema.parse throws a ZodError, and the real need is knowing why validation failed. Use safeParse (or catch ZodError) and log error.issues (paths, codes, messages), which do not contain submitted values by default. Return a 400 with the field errors. Note that parse() throwing inside an async Express handler may also result in an unhandled rejection or 500 depending on the Express version and error middleware, so handling it explicitly would fix a likely cause of the 'failed signups' being opaque.

findings.title: Logging at info level on every signup attempt adds noise and volume
findings.explanation: This logs every attempt, including successes, at info level. If any diagnostic logging is retained, restrict it to the failure path (warn level) and consider rate limiting or sampling, since signup endpoints are public and attackers can inflate log volume with large bodies. Also ensure body size limits are enforced upstream.

findings.title: Unbounded attacker-controlled data in logs (log injection / size)
findings.explanation: The endpoint is unauthenticated, so the logged body is fully attacker-controlled: arbitrarily large or deeply nested values and strings with control characters. Even with a structured logger, this can bloat logs or pollute them. Log truncated, allow-listed fields only.

findings.title: Missing tests for the redaction assumption
findings.explanation: If any payload logging is kept, add a test asserting that password and similar variants never appear in log output, rather than relying on the statement that the logger already redacts them.
